caption:
Anthropic agreed to pay $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of Caterpillar gas generators, the Financial Times reported.
It took over orders a Texas supplier placed about two years ago, while new equipment now takes years to arrive.
The FT calls it the biggest known single power equipment purchase by an AI company.

Should AI companies run their own gas power?

threads_text: Anthropic reportedly paid $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of gas generators a Texas supplier ordered years ago. When new power equipment takes years to arrive, AI labs just buy someone else's place in line. Should AI companies be running their own gas power?

paragraphs.text: Anthropic has agreed to pay $3.4 billion for gas-fired generators to power its data centers, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, November 8, 2026. According to the report, the purchase covers 1.7 gigawatts of large generators, and the FT described it as the largest known single purchase of power equipment by an AI company.

The agreement was signed in late September with OnePWR Solutions, a power equipment supplier based in San Antonio, Texas. Both Anthropic and OnePWR declined to comment to the FT, and The Next Web noted that it had not independently confirmed the deal.

OnePWR had ordered the generators from Caterpillar roughly two years earlier but needed financing to complete the purchase, according to the report. Anthropic had first planned to buy electricity from OnePWR. It instead took over the equipment orders along with the engineering and construction work needed to install the machines.

Anthropic did not acquire OnePWR itself, and none of the supplier’s employees moved to Anthropic, a person familiar with the matter told the FT. Separately, a transaction listing from the investment bank Piper Sandler, which advised OnePWR, shows a $3.4 billion sale of the company’s power generation platform to an unnamed AI lab in September. The listing does not name Anthropic.

The FT reported that the engines were ordered before prices for such equipment surged and that they can be delivered in the near term and over the next two years, while manufacturing lead times for new orders now stretch years into the future. The report did not say where the generators will be installed or which data centers they will serve.
Part of a much larger buildout

The purchase comes as Anthropic prepares for a stock market listing. The company disclosed on November 2 that it expects to spend more than $895 billion in the years ahead, almost all of it on computing capacity and related infrastructure.

In a policy announcement in February, Anthropic pledged to pay for the grid upgrades needed to connect its data centers, to bring new generation online to match their electricity use, and to cover increases in consumer electricity prices attributable to those facilities. According to The Energy Mag, those commitments apply where Anthropic develops data centers with partners for its own workloads; for capacity it leases in existing facilities, the company said it is exploring other ways to address the effect on power prices.

Other AI companies have also turned to gas to bring data centers online quickly. Elon Musk’s xAI bought mobile gas turbines earlier in 2026 for $2 billion and faces a lawsuit over turbines at its site in Memphis, while Alphabet bought the energy developer Intersect in late 2025.

For NeuraFeed, the notable detail is less the price than the method. By taking over orders that were already in the queue, Anthropic appears to have bought time as much as hardware. At $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts, the deal works out to roughly $2,000 per kilowatt, though the reports do not say how the total splits between equipment and installation work. The move also places Anthropic among AI developers that rely on fossil fuel generation to meet near-term demand, which may draw attention to how it squares the purchase with its February energy pledge.

The next detail to watch is where the 1.7 gigawatts of generators are installed, since the location will show which Anthropic data centers they serve and how the company applies its pledge on local electricity prices.
